newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish shares fall, seen extending loss.
newsitem.headline: Polish shares fall, seen extending loss.

text.p: Polish shares on Thursday fell after a two-day gain and analysts said the main market, now at 17,414.8 points, would apparently fall more after having gained 38 percent from mid-December to mid-February, analysts said.

"There's been no radical overvaluing for us to expect a big correction...but definitely we'll have a correction of about 10 percent to 16,000 points," said Michal Szczurek, an analyst at ING BSK Asset Management.
Other analysts said 17,000 points would more likely provide support. Analysts said small-cap stocks, recent leaders, had joined blue chips in performing poorly.

The main market's all-share WIG index fell 2.3 percent to 17,414.8 points and turnover fell 36 percent to 154.5 million zlotys ($50.2 million) on all three markets. Losers led gainers by 77 to seven with six stocks flat.
Espebepe tumbled 9.8 percent the day before the builder's creditors meet to discuss a possible debt write off. The bourse has suspended trade in the stock on Friday.
Five other main market stocks fell at least nine percent.
Loss leaders in active trade included computer maker Optimus and trader Universal after recent big gains.
Analysts said top gainer car maker Debica, up 4.9 percent, was buoyed by Wednesday's news it had significantly increased net profits for the second month running.
They said upcoming large public offerings by food trader and producer Agros and paper firm Celuloza Swiecie SA could draw capital from listed shares and limit growth potential.
NFI units fell 2.2 percent at the regular session and rose 0.6 percent in continuous trade, where the WIG 20 index lost 1.4 percent.
